common_name: Ruby Ball Cabbage (1960 AAS-Winning Early Red Hybrid Cabbage)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; in zone 9, set out transplants in late summer for a fall crop or in very early spring for a quick spring harvest before summer heat arrives. The compact, uniformly round heads mature quickly and hold in the garden for a week or two past maturity without splitting.

directions: Start seeds indoors six to eight weeks before the planned transplant date, then set hardened-off seedlings into full sun in fertile, well-drained soil. Ruby Ball is an F1 hybrid red cabbage that won an All-America Selections award in 1960 for its ability to form small, dense, perfectly round purple-red heads earlier and more uniformly than the open-pollinated red cabbages that were standard at the time. The compact three- to four-pound heads are notably crack-resistant and hold in the garden for a week or two past maturity, giving some flexibility in harvest timing. Like other red cabbages, Ruby Ball carries a sharper, slightly peppery flavor and higher anthocyanin content than green types, and it is well suited to coleslaw, quick braises, and short-term cold storage.
